CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE GAUTAM KUMAR CHOUDHARY -----
For the Appellant : Mr. Amit Kr. Sinha, Advocate
For the State : Mr. Sunil Kr. Dubey, APP
For Respondent No.2 : Mr. A.K. Sahani, Advocate -----
Oral Order 11 / Dated : 16.04.2024 Heard the parties.

1. Instant criminal appeal has been filed under Section 14A(2) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2015 against the order dated 11.04.2023 passed in Complaint Case No. 77 of 2021 under Section 420 of Indian Penal Code and Section 3(1)(r)(s) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989,
whereby and where under the anticipatory bail of the appellant was rejected.

sentences.text: 2. As per the complaint case, which has been filed against the appellant, is that after completing her education, she was in search of employment and found an advertisement on the boundary wall for getting service of Rs.15,000/- to Rs.25,000/-.

3. Complainant contacted and met Punit Bansal at Ratu Road, Indrapuri, Nawab Rai Lane on contacting him on his mobile, and she was promised to get employment of Rs. 15,000/- per month which was to be increased to Rs. 20,000/- subsequently.

It is alleged that she started working in the shop on 01.07.2021 but she was paid only Rs. 2,000/- and when he did not make the payment of promised salary, she asked the appellant to give the salary due as promise, she was abused by calling her caste name and the balance of Rs. 40,000 was not paid.

sentences.text: 4. During enquiry, the complainant and two other witnesses were examined.
Thereafter the process was issued against the appellant.

5. It is submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that the appellant has no connection with Ranchi and he had never established any shop in Ranchi and as per the report, received in pursuance of the order passed by this Court, there was no such office under the name of Swastik Enterprises in the said place at Ratu Road, Indrapuri under Sukhdeo Nagar Police Station.

It is further submitted that the complainant herself has stated in the solemn affirmation that the instant case has been filed to recover the balance amount and therefore the offence under SC/ST Prevention of Atrocities Act will not be attracted in view of the ratio as laid down in Ramawatar v. State of M.P.,
(2022) 13 SCC 635.
6.

entities.text:
Ramawatar v. State of M.P.,
(2022) 13 SCC 635
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the State assisted by learned counsel for the complainant, have opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that in para 8 there is specific allegation of abusing the complainant by calling her by caste name.
It is further submitted that the allegation has been reiterated in para 1 of the solemn affirmation 7.
Complaint petition is silent about the date on which the complainant was abused and castiest remarks were made against her.
Complaint petition predominantly is about salary due.
Under the circumstance the impugned order set aside.

Appellant named above in the event of his arrest or surrender within a period of three weeks from the date of this order, shall be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Court below.
Criminal appeal is allowed.

(Gautam Kumar Choudhary, J.) AKT/Satendra Uploaded Punit Bansal vs The State Of Jharkhand on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105289580/
